text.p: Supporters of 105 VIP hostages held in Lima are turning to the Internet to demand the release of the captives trapped in the Japanese ambassador's residence.

By Christmas day on Wednesday, 1,318 Internet users from around the world had signed a special "solidarity list" posted on the Internet calling for the freedom of the hostages and "energetically condemning" their seizure.

Local Internet supplier, the Peruvian Scientific Network, has set up a special page for the captives who were taken hostage by Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels eight days ago while attending a party at the Japanese ambassador's home.

"As Peruvians, we feel ashamed because our compatriots have cast a shadow over the world community," the network's statement said. It called on foreign supporters, families of victims and Peruvians to unite and "demand a bloodless and humane solution to this serious problem."
The Cuban-inspired MRTA also uses the Internet to get across its message. The Marxist rebel group publishes its radical magazines "Rebel Voice" and "Change" via the Internet.
